{"id":"JMAP-jfia.19","title":"HandlerFuture output Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError> is anonymous tuple, cannot grow","description":"crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:73-74 — HandlerFuture is defined as:

    pub type HandlerFuture =
        Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>> + Send>>;

The `Output = Result<(Value, Vec<Invocation>), JmapError>` shape is the
return type of every JmapHandler::call. The (Value, Vec<Invocation>)
tuple is anonymous — no struct wrapper, no #[non_exhaustive] surface,
no way to add a third field without breaking every existing handler
impl.

What callers cannot depend on: that the handler return shape can grow.
A future feature — handler-emitted metrics, panic-occurrence flag,
per-call timing, retry hint for the dispatcher, etc. — cannot be added
to the trait method's return shape without:

1. A major-version bump
2. Migration of every JmapHandler impl in every extension *-server
   crate (8 today, more planned)
3. Migration of every ClosureHandler closure in every register_*_handlers
   macro across consumers

What goes wrong when this stays as-is: by the time the kit needs to
return one more piece of data per handler call (the existing `extra
invocations` parameter is already the second member of this tuple,
which is itself evidence the original `Value`-only shape was wrong),
the cost of adding it has already crystallised at every callsite.

Resolution: replace the tuple with a named #[non_exhaustive] struct,
e.g.:

    pub struct HandlerOutput {
        pub primary: Value,
        pub extra_invocations: Vec<Invocation>,
        // future fields land here non-breakingly
    }
    pub type HandlerFuture =
        Pin<Box<dyn Future<Output = Result<HandlerOutput, JmapError>> + Send>>;

The pre-major-bump cost of this rename is ~7 extension *-server crates
that all just landed under JMAP-wlip. The post-major-bump cost of NOT
doing this is structurally unbounded because each future field forces
the same propagation pass.

This is the kit's first major opportunity to convert "tuple-of-two"
into "named-struct-of-N" before the type ossifies.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-05-14T16:45:10Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-05-14T17:10:53Z","metadata":{},"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"","depends_on_id":"","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-05-14T09:45:10Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"DECISION NEEDED (triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf): Question for Mark: should the handler return type change from the tuple `(Value, Vec<Invocation>)` to a named `#[non_exhaustive]` struct HandlerOutput { primary, extra_invocations }? Every JmapHandler impl and register_*_handlers closure in 8 crates (143 sites) would break. If yes, when?
Options:
(a) Do it now as a breaking 0.2→0.3 change across the workspace, in one mechanical pass over about 41 files. Because the struct is #[non_exhaustive], extension crates can't build it with a struct literal, so it also needs constructors `HandlerOutput::new(primary)` and `.with_extra(vec)`.
(b) Keep it deferred until a concrete need for a third field shows up (metrics, retry hint) or a planned major bump, and land it under that epic. This is the status quo, with the bead labeled deferred.
(c) Migrate in two steps: add HandlerOutput plus a `From<(Value, Vec<Invocation>)>` impl and have the dispatcher accept both shapes for one cycle, then sweep the crates one at a time. The transition shim makes this the most code of the three.
Recommendation: (a) if the workspace is still pre-1.0 and the crates are only used inside it. At 0.x a minor bump is already allowed to break, the change is mechanical (size L by line count, low risk), and the cost of doing it later keeps growing as crates are added. Otherwise (b), which is the existing ratified deferral. Either way, reject (c): it adds a transition shim for no gain.
Tests if (a) is chosen: the existing dispatcher tests should pass unchanged in behaviour. The independent oracle is the RFC 8621 §7.5 onSuccessUpdateEmail ordering: the implicit Email/set response must come right after the EmailSubmission/set response in methodResponses."}
